details:
=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/orchestrate_force_tick.sh:33-40 | severity=low | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro]
  PROBLEM: `_force_tick_tracking_issue_from_ref` is defined but never invoked in the tracking-issue resolution flow.
  WHY: It is dead code in the current dispatch path, so it adds unused logic without affecting runtime behavior.
- scripts/orchestrate_force_tick.sh:44-48 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m2_5]
  PROBLEM: The tracking issue extraction regex can match partial text instead of requiring a full branch-name match.
  WHY: A branch like `feature/orchestrator/project-999-extra` can be treated as `orchestrator/project-999`, which dispatches the wrong tracking issue.
- scripts/orchestrate_force_tick.sh:306-306 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: The branch-ref tracking issue extractor can accept branch names that merely contain the `orchestrator/project-<id>` pattern.
  WHY: Both reviewers show the extractor can pull the wrong issue ID from a PR branch, which writes cooldown/dispatch state for the wrong orchestrator project.
- scripts/memory_helpers.sh:500-502 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: `_memory_force_tick_remote_branch_exists` uses an unanchored grep pattern that can match substrings.
  WHY: A branch like `ai-memory-cooldown` can be mistaken for `ai-memory`, producing a false positive existence check.
- scripts/render_prompt.sh:44-66 | severity=medium | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: The placeholder renderer can leave workflow placeholders unexpanded and pass them through to the backend.
  WHY: Templates containing `{{WORKFLOW_EDIT_RESTRICTION}}`, `{{SEMBLE_PREFETCH}}`, or `{{SERENA_TOOL_HINTS}}` can reach the backend literally, producing malformed prompts.
- scripts/orchestrate_force_tick.sh:328-380 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: A run with `FORCE_TICK_ENABLED=false` persists a `disabled` record that later suppresses legitimate force-tick dispatches after the feature is re-enabled.
  WHY: The cooldown gate checks only timestamps and does not distinguish disabled records, so the first post-reenable dispatch is skipped until the cooldown window expires.
- scripts/memory_helpers.sh:734-752 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: Concurrent force-tick runs can both pass the cooldown gate and dispatch before any claim becomes visible.
  WHY: The collision wrapper and subsequent re-read are not atomic across separate clones, so two dispatches can fire for the same tracking issue within the cooldown window.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===
- requirement: "Files in scope (stay inside this set)" lists nine specific files; scripts/render_prompt.sh is not one of them.
  expected_change_site: scripts/render_prompt.sh should not have been modified in this PR.
  confidence=5
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5]
  EVIDENCE: LAST RUN DIFF and PR DIFF both show substantial modifications to scripts/render_prompt.sh (delegation to render_prompt.py backend / 77 lines changed).
- requirement: "Keep the matching listed workflow-template wrappers in sync where this issue already names them."
  expected_change_site: workflow-templates/ai-implement.yml, workflow-templates/ai-review.yml, workflow-templates/ai-validate.yml
  confidence=5
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  EVIDENCE: No diff hunks modify any file under workflow-templates/; PR DIFF and LAST RUN DIFF contain no modifications.
- requirement: "Tests cover cooldown/no-op behavior and the dispatch payload shape" AND the repo CI runs an explicit allowlist of `python3 tests/<file>.py` invocations.
  expected_change_site: .github/workflows/test-and-mark-stable.yml (or equivalent CI configuration) adding invocation of tests/test_orchestrate_force_tick.py
  confidence=4
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  EVIDENCE: grep for test_orchestrate_force_tick across all `.github/workflows/*.yml` returns zero matches; existing explicit test invocations do not include `tests/test_orchestrate_force_tick.py`.
- requirement: "Tests cover cooldown/no-op behavior and the dispatch payload shape."
  expected_change_site: tests/test_orchestrate_force_tick.py
  confidence=3
  flagged_by: [x-ai_grok-4_20]
  EVIDENCE: The test does not exercise the permanent-suppression case after a disabled run, and it does not assert the rendered payload exactly matches the orchestrator poller shape / ai-memory schemas.
=== END CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- scripts/orchestrate_force_tick.sh:33-40 | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: `_force_tick_tracking_issue_from_ref` is defined but never invoked in the tracking-issue resolution flow.
  WHY: The actual resolution path uses `_force_tick_extract_tracking_issue_from_pull_request_json` and `_force_tick_extract_tracking_issue`, so this helper never affects runtime behavior.
- scripts/orchestrate_force_tick.sh:130-148, 335-345 | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: When `FORCE_TICK_ENABLED=false`, the script writes a `disabled` record with the current timestamp, and the cooldown gate later ignores `dispatch_status`.
  WHY: Re-enabling the flag within the cooldown window makes the first legitimate force-tick attempt look like an ordinary cooldown hit and suppresses dispatch until the window expires.
- scripts/orchestrate_force_tick.sh and scripts/memory_helpers.sh: orchestrator line 310 and lines 355-381; memory_helpers.sh lines 745-752 | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: Two concurrent force-tick runs for the same tracking issue can both pass the initial `_force_tick_latest_gate_tsv` check before either run's `memory_force_tick_put` commits its pending record.
  WHY: The collision wrapper only catches some interleavings after a clone/push boundary; two separate clones can still both end up claiming and dispatching within the cooldown window.
- Requirement: "Files in scope (stay inside this set)" lists nine specific files; scripts/render_prompt.sh is not one of them.
  Expected change site: scripts/render_prompt.sh should not have been modified in this PR.
  Evidence of absence: LAST RUN DIFF and PR DIFF both show substantial modifications to scripts/render_prompt.sh (replacing inline placeholder replacement with delegation to render_prompt.py backend, 77 lines changed).
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
- Requirement: "Tests cover cooldown/no-op behavior and the dispatch payload shape" (acceptance criteria). The repository's CI (test-and-mark-stable.yml) runs an explicit allowlist of `python3 tests/<file>.py` invocations with no auto-discovery.
  Expected change site: .github/workflows/test-and-mark-stable.yml (or equivalent CI configuration) adding an invocation of tests/test_orchestrate_force_tick.py
  Evidence of absence: grep for test_orchestrate_force_tick across all .github/workflows/*.yml returns zero matches. The existing test invocations at lines 2163-2166 and 3287-3292 of test-and-mark-stable.yml list other test files explicitly but do not include test_orchestrate_force_tick.py. Without a CI invocation, test coverage can silently regress on every subsequent change.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
=== END FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m2_5 ===
- scripts/orchestrate_force_tick.sh:44-48 | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The tracking issue extraction regex is not anchored to the full branch name, allowing partial matches.
  WHY: A branch like `feature/orchestrator/project-999-extra` could match `orchestrator/project-999` via the substring pattern, causing the wrong tracking issue to be dispatched.
- scripts/memory_helpers.sh:734-752 | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The collision wrapper does not atomically update the stored record before the bash caller proceeds, allowing concurrent force-tick calls to both pass the cooldown gate.
  WHY: Two simultaneous phase-end dispatches for the same tracking issue can both read the cooldown state before either writes, resulting in duplicate workflow dispatches.
- scripts/orchestrate_force_tick.sh:328-344 | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: When FORCE_TICK_ENABLED=false, a disabled record is persisted that permanently suppresses later dispatches even after re-enabling.
  WHY: Setting `FORCE_TICK_ENABLED=false` then back to `true` does not reset the cooldown; the existing record with `dispatch_status: "disabled"` still blocks dispatch because the cooldown check doesn't distinguish disabled from active records.
- Requirement: "Keep the matching listed workflow-template wrappers in sync where this issue already names them."
  Expected change site: workflow-templates/ai-implement.yml, workflow-templates/ai-review.yml, workflow-templates/ai-validate.yml
  Evidence of absence: No modifications to any workflow-templates/*.yml files in PR DIFF or LAST RUN DIFF. The editor noted they are "thin @stable delegates" but the acceptance criteria explicitly requires keeping them in sync.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
- Requirement: "Tests cover cooldown/no-op behavior and the dispatch payload shape" AND repository CI runs an explicit allowlist of test invocations.
  Expected change site: .github/workflows/test.yml or similar to invoke tests/test_orchestrate_force_tick.py
  Evidence of absence: The test file exists but is not added to any CI workflow invocation list. The repo uses explicit `python3 tests/<file>.py` calls with no discovery, so this test will not run in CI.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
- Requirement: "Files in scope (stay inside this set)" - the linked issue lists specific files; modifications must remain within that set.
  Expected change site: scripts/render_prompt.sh should NOT be modified
  Evidence of absence: LAST RUN DIFF shows significant modifications to scripts/render_prompt.sh (77 lines changed) even though it's not in the permitted file set for S3.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m2_5 ===

  PROBLEM: The branch-ref tracking issue extractor can accept branch names that merely contain the `orchestrator/project-<id>` pattern.
  WHY: A PR branch can yield the wrong tracking issue ID, so the orchestrator writes cooldown/dispatch state for an unrelated project.
- scripts/memory_helpers.sh:734-752 and orchestrate_force_tick.sh lines 355-385 | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The collision check is not atomic, so two concurrent calls can both pass the cooldown check before either writes.
  WHY: The `memory_force_tick_get`/`memory_force_tick_put` gap allows duplicate workflow dispatches and violates idempotency.
- scripts/orchestrate_force_tick.sh:370-380 | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: Persisting a `dispatch_status="disabled"` record when `FORCE_TICK_ENABLED=false` causes later re-enabled runs to be blocked by the cooldown gate.
  WHY: The gate treats any existing record as a hit regardless of status, so the next legitimate dispatch is skipped until cooldown expiry.
